title: There's a Shark That Can Live for 400 Years

scenes.text: There's a shark that can live for 400 years.
The oldest Greenland shark ever tested was about 392 years old. It hatched in the sixteen hundreds, long before the United States existed.
It grows about one centimeter a year, and a female isn't ready to have pups until she's roughly 150.
How do we know? Scientists carbon-dated the center of its eye lens, which forms before birth and never changes.
It lives in near-freezing Arctic water, so everything about it runs slow: its heartbeat, its growth, its aging.
That makes it the longest-living animal with a backbone. Would you want to be a teenager at age 100?

description:
There's a shark that can live for 400 years.
In 2016, scientists carbon-dated the eye lenses of Greenland sharks and found the oldest was about 392 years old, making it the longest-living vertebrate known. Females don't mature until around 150.
Would you want to be a teenager at age 100?
